openingMessage: In leadership, there are no words more important than trust.
openingWhy: When you write 0 ppm on a form, the next crew opens that line without re-testing — your signature is their gas test. Fudge one reading and every number you've ever signed becomes a question. There's no re-cal for a hand nobody trusts.
leadershipThought: When a location falls behind, a monitor isn't charged, a tube isn't signed out — the question isn't whose fault is it. The question is: what can I do about it now? The moment you stop blaming, you gain control.

specialFocus.title: Keep the Good Fight Up: This Week's Catches
specialFocus.why:
Caleb, last one before Thanksgiving. Keep the good fight up. Today is about the catches: real ones, off our own OWL forms, from the last week.

“We're in the same fight together. We all want the best for our families and ourselves. Stay diligent, keep your head on a swivel, and watch each other's backs.”
— Mike Lyons

Look at the first two. A loose connection with pressure behind it, and a leaking nipple. That's this week's topic, Energy Isolation, caught by people who were paying attention. Nobody had to learn it the hard way.

✓ THE CATCHES: say these names
  • Dawson Drake and Robert Henigan, Mabee Foundation G #2 (Fri): the flow line connection was loose and the tubing still had pressure on it. They didn't go ahead with the job, and it got rescheduled. Matt's review: “the stop was the right call.”
  • Kedrick McCarter and Hayden Haugh, University 58-17B 2H (Thu 11/19): a nipple was leaking. It got changed out, and both of their forms say so. Same leak, same story, two forms.
  • Michael Jobe, Stone Robb E45A 1H (Fri): no spotter, no forklift. Jobe stopped it until the vest and flag were there.
  • Alfredo Vaquera, Cass Countiss 20G 7H (Mon): saw the forklift moving, and wrote down how the crew controlled it: good communication with the driver, and a tag line. Name the hazard, then name the control.
  • Humberto Marquez-Salazar at Kyle 2600 and Pablo Soto at Windham R #3 (Mon): one well had no sign, the other's was incomplete. Both got a picture to identify the location.
⭐ DOING IT RIGHT: Monday
  • Justin Pack, Hughes #1: another complete daily, every photo from that day.
  • Justin Fontenot: two air jobs, Locklar Holiman and Turner E41C, with Observe, Win and Learn all filled in.
  • Kyle Williams and Chris Cochren: three training classes between them, all closed out complete.
▲ KEEP THE GOOD FIGHT UP: three for today
  • See it, say it, write it. Every catch on this list made it onto a form. That's how the next crew finds out.
  • Didn't go ahead? That's a stop. If the job stopped, or never started because of what you saw, tick “utilized.” You earned it.
  • Fresh eyes on every job. New well, new form, your own words. Then get home to your people.
Ten minutes: Mike's words (1) · the catches (4) · Monday's names (1) · three asks (1) · the scenario (2) · send-off (1).
specialFocus.standardLabel: Week 24: Energy Isolation, Look Before You Touch It
standard: Walk it first. Connections, valves, gauges and the sign, before any tool comes out.
Loose, leaking or not what you expected? Don't touch it. Call it, and tell the company man.
Treat it as live until it's bled, read and proven zero.
Rescheduled is a good outcome. Tell the next crew exactly what you found.
Both partners write it. Same catch, two forms, your own words.

scenarios.title: "It's Just a Little Loose"
scenarios.body: It's the last job before Thanksgiving. Walking the line, you find a connection that's loose with pressure still behind it. Somebody says, “It's just a little loose, we'll snug it up and go.” What do you do? Hands off, call the hold, tell the company man, and let it get bled down and fixed right. If that means it's rescheduled, brief the next crew on what you found. Caleb, ask the circle: who's had a call like that, and who backed you up?

questions: Which of these catches could have been on your job? Would you have seen it?
What did your partner catch this week that nobody else knows about?
Who are you thankful for on this crew? Tell them before you roll.
specialFocus.nonNegotiable: Look before you touch, stop it when it's wrong, and watch each other's backs. Same fight, same team. Happy Thanksgiving. We all go home.
